📝 Notes
Mar 12, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
The team discussed prototype development, generative UI exploration, and funding opportunities for Mycelium, alongside the setup of analytics and a briefing on a hacker/research lab.Brainstorming and Prototype ExplorationPrototypes for the Sur project are moving forward, with a plan to explore Unison’s generative UI for visualizing data from the Brain. Boyd is seeking funding opportunities for Mycelium, focusing on broad research and already finding a 100,000 application opportunity.Analytics Setup and FunctionalityAnalytics were successfully set up using a self-hostable, open-source tool connected to the Postgress database, currently operating at 60% capacity. The tool creates prefixed views for data sharing with Melissa and will be deployed to the real database today.Reviewing External Projects and SafetyA discussion on a San Francisco-based hacker/research lab highlighted its focus on experimental projects, AI, and brain-computer interfaces. A meeting is scheduled for tomorrow at 12:45 to discuss Cibil safety regulations.
Details
Status and Prototype Brainstorming: Amir Houieh reported being busy with the Sur project, having completed work for the Brain, and writing a post draft. They are planning to start working on a visual prototype today but are currently unsure what to make, noting a feeling of reduced creativity and desire to materialize existing ideas (00:00:00) (00:07:36). Gabor Kerekes shared that they experienced a similar motivational slump earlier in the year but are now feeling motivated again (00:08:28).
Generative UI Exploration with Unison: Noémi Biró and Gabor Kerekes proposed that Amir Houieh could explore using Unison’s generative UI, noting that it is easy and does not require extensive knowledge of Unison. Gabor Kerekes suggested that this effort could focus on visualizing data from the Brain by designing a system that designs the UI, rather than designing the UI directly, and offered to help set up the necessary repo after the meeting (00:06:14).
Funding Opportunities for Mycelium: Noémi Biró updated the team on having sent Melissa the discussed resources and mentioned plans to research funding opportunities for Mycelium. Based on a discussion with Boyd, Noémi Biró intends to conduct a broad search, noting that Boyd is part of a board that evaluates funding proposals, particularly in VR and AR research, and knows there are many opportunities in the Netherlands, Romania, and Hungary (00:08:28). Noémi Biró has already found one 10-minute, 100,000 application opportunity and will send it over (00:10:21).
Discussing Hacker/Research Labs and Support for Projects: Gabor Kerekes provided context on a San Francisco-based hacker/research lab that supports experimental projects, explaining that the original meaning of "hacker" refers to people who tinker and build out of curiosity. This lab focuses on AI, brain-computer interfaces, and supporting projects that might not receive funding from VCs (00:10:21). Gabor Kerekes reflected on the need for a shared bookmarking tool, which they are currently trying to implement (00:12:00).
Upcoming Safety Regulations Meeting and Preparation: Gabor Kerekes scheduled a meeting with Melissa for tomorrow at 12:45 to discuss safety regulations related to Cibil. They proposed that the team sync tomorrow after the daily meeting to align on questions, and Amir Houieh committed to spending an hour today reviewing the material (00:13:22).
Software Factory and Analytics Setup: Gabor Kerekes reported that the software factory is operating at 60% or 70% capacity but is expecting an increase with a new sandbox version. They were able to set up analytics by prompting a few times, choosing a self-hostable, open-source tool that connects to the local development Postgress database and supports making dashboards (00:13:22). The tool was selected because it offers an MCP and good documentation for agents to interact with the API and set up SQL queries (00:14:51).
Analytics Dashboard Functionality and Deployment: Gabor Kerekes clarified that the analytics tool creates prefixed views and data streams to be shipped to Melissa, allowing them to see what data they are missing, rather than supporting arbitrary, on-demand query visualization via open-source tools. The goal is to avoid sending weekly exports by having Melissa download data directly or use the Google Sheets integration, which syncs SQL query results periodically (00:16:25). Gabor Kerekes emphasized that the dashboard was set up in two minutes and aims to connect the tool to the real database and deploy it today (00:19:32) (00:23:29).
Discussion on Natural Language to SQL Generation: Amir Houieh questioned whether there are open-source tools for natural language to SQL query generation and visualization on demand, noting the analytics tool seems to focus on visualization on top of a MySQL database (00:19:32). Gabor Kerekes confirmed that while the tool has a co-pilot feature for this, it is only available with an enterprise license, although they noted that Cloud or Chat GPT can easily generate the necessary SQL (00:20:45) (00:23:29). They concluded that the current fixed-view solution is already a significant step forward and meets the immediate need for analytics (00:22:15).
Feedback and Editing of Social Media Post: Unbody io requested feedback on a social media post draft they sent on Discord, asking Gabor Kerekes to feel free to edit it today. Unbody io suggested making the call to action clearer, for example, inviting people to join or bring their projects and challenges (00:23:29). Gabor Kerekes agreed, suggesting making it explicit that they are accepting projects and detailing what they can offer, such as developing prototypes, MVPs, or consultancy services like workshops (00:25:16).
Next Steps for Brainstorming and Analytics Deployment: Amir Houieh committed to spending a couple of hours today brainstorming and listing a few product ideas to build on top of the Brain to break out of a fine-tuning loop. Gabor Kerekes stated they would start deploying the analytics tool and connecting it to the real database to have real data to show by tomorrow, which they believe will be beneficial for the team (00:26:30).
Suggested next steps
Gabor Kerekes will deploy the analytics tool today and connect it to the real database to have real data by Friday.
Gabor Kerekes will help Amir Houieh set up the generative UI of Unison after the meeting and share the repo.
Noémi Biró will look into funding opportunities for myelium, gather resources, and send over the funding application found last week.
Gabor Kerekes will edit the social media post to make the call to action clear about accepting projects.
Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes will look at the safety regulations today, spending about an hour on it.
Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes will sync tomorrow after daily to go over the questions regarding the safety regulations.
